description: Verify that DUT discards an IPv4 packet whose header checksum is wrong — checksum mismatch means the header is corrupt and the packet is unsafe to act on (RFC 1071 + RFC 791 §3.1)
approach:
[Objective]
The IPv4 header carries a one's-complement checksum over the header words (RFC 1071). Any single-bit error in the header is detected by this checksum. A mismatch means the header is corrupt; trusting it could route the packet wrong, deliver it to the wrong protocol, or trigger overreads.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet to DUT IP, header_checksum intentionally wrong (e.g. last bit flipped)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any response.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT responded despite the bad header checksum. Indicates receive path skipped checksum verification.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the bad-checksum packet — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT responded despite invalid IPv4 checksum — verification skipped
